Watch_Dogs 2 is a third person open world action/stealth game that takes the few things that were good about the first Watch_Dogs and pumps them up to 11.

The game controls great, the free running is much more fluid, there's tons more side content and just general stuff to do. San Fransisco looks beautiful and it's actually insane how good this game still looks 10 years after release.

The city is more vibrant and has more interesting locales than Watch_Dogs 1 and is really fun to roam around in and find stuff. It reminded me why the "Ubisoft open world" got so popular in the first place - when it's done well, it's a really fun playground!

One of my biggest gripes about Watch_Dogs 1 was the overly edgy writing - this has been toned down in the sequel, albeit it's been replaced with what some might call "millenial cringe". Personally, I found it fun - a real time-capsule of the mid 2010s. The cast is fun and all the personalities are interesting without becoming grating caricatures

Another thing they really improved on in the second game is the stealth. You now have actual options for it and just mowing down a whole compound of enemies is reasonably harder than in the first game. The quadcopter and jumper provide a lot of versatility for approaching encounters and there were some missions that to my great glee I managed to complete without ever setting foot in the restricted area

All in all, if you miss the days when open worlds were cool instead of tiring busy-work, then I suggest getting this game on sale! It's great fun

Watch Dogs 2 is a pretty decent game and I had a good time playing it, but I wouldn't call it anything special. The story is okay, the characters are interesting enough, and the open world is fun to explore at first, but the game has quite a few problems that keep it from being great.

One of the best things about the game is definitely the main missions. There are some genuinely fun moments, and Robot Wars was easily my favorite mission in the entire game. It was creative, entertaining, and actually felt different from the usual missions. Unfortunately, most of the other missions follow pretty much the same formula: break into a building, hack something, get the information you need, and leave. The hacking itself is fun initially, especially when you use drones and different gadgets to avoid enemies, but it gets repetitive after a while. I really wish there were more types of hacking mechanics and more variety in how you approach objectives.

I also tried a few side missions, but honestly, most of them were pretty trash and didn't really motivate me to keep playing them. The open world has plenty of activities, but quantity doesn't always mean quality.

The characters are decent, and Ray was easily my favorite. He has a lot of personality and brings some entertaining moments to the story. Dusan, on the other hand, reminded me a bit of Joseph Seed from Far Cry 5, both in appearance and behavior. The story itself is okay, but I never found it particularly amazing or memorable.

Driving isn't bad either, and the cars handle well enough, but I barely used them because fast travel was simply more convenient. I honestly don't think I've ever gone somewhere without using fast travel unless a mission forced me to drive. The city looks great, though, and exploring San Francisco is enjoyable, especially with all the hacking opportunities and things you can interact with.

I also like that the game gives you different ways to approach certain situations. You can sneak around, use your gadgets, distract enemies, or go in more aggressively if things go wrong. Playing stealthily and using your tools creatively can be really satisfying, even if the underlying objectives start feeling repetitive.

Overall, Watch Dogs 2 is worth playing, especially if you enjoy open-world games and messing around with hacking mechanics. It has some great moments, likable characters, and a fun setting, but the repetitive missions and underwhelming side content hold it back. It's a good enough game, just not one I'd consider particularly memorable.

For me, the first Watch Dogs is still clearly superior, especially in terms of story, atmosphere, and the overall experience. Watch Dogs 2 is more colorful and playful, but I personally prefer the darker tone of the original.

Final verdict: 7/10. A fun game that's worth trying, but it could have been so much better with more mission variety and a stronger story.

reviews.review:
**Played on PS4 in 2021, now giving it another chance on PC**

I first started playing Watch Dogs 2 on PS4 on April 17, 2021, but stopped playing on July 12, 2021. Back then, I probably just lost interest after playing for a while and moved on to other games. Sometimes you leave a game unfinished, not because it's bad, but because you feel like playing something else.

Now I've decided to give it another chance on Steam. I want to revisit San Francisco, enjoy the hacking mechanics again, and experience the game from a fresh perspective on PC.

It's interesting coming back to a game I played years ago and remembering an experience I left behind. This time, I hope to enjoy it again and maybe finally get further into the game than I did on PS4.

**Recommended.** Sometimes it's worth coming back to an old game and giving it another chance.

[h3] A Different Side of Watch Dogs [/h3]

Watch Dogs 2 is one of those games that makes you appreciate how much personality an open world can have. Coming back to the series after the first game, it's interesting to see how different the sequel feels while still keeping what made the original enjoyable. San Francisco is a fantastic setting, full of life, colour and things to discover. Exploring the city never really gets old, and the soundtrack fits the atmosphere brilliantly, giving the game its own identity and making the world feel alive. One of my favourite parts is the story and the DedSec crew. The characters each have their own personalities, and their interactions bring plenty of humour and charm. Although the tone is much lighter than the first game, the story still explores interesting ideas about privacy, surveillance and the power of technology. It makes you want to see what happens next. The gameplay is another highlight. The hacking mechanics give you plenty of freedom in how you approach missions, while the RC Jumper and Quadcopter make things even more enjoyable. Experimenting with different approaches keeps the gameplay fresh throughout. Of course, the game isn't perfect. Some of the humour doesn't always land, and parts of the story feel a little uneven, but these issues don't take away from the overall experience. Overall, Watch Dogs 2 is a brilliant sequel that takes the series in a different direction and makes it work. With a memorable cast, an incredible setting and entertaining gameplay, it's a game that's easy to get lost in. It may feel very different from the original, but that's exactly what makes it stand out.
